title: The Lærdal Tunnel - Nordge
content: # Sunrise and Northern Lights in the Lærdal Tunnel. Lærdalstunnelen is the world's longest road tunnel, 24,5 km long, connecting Lærdal to Aurland in Sogn og Fjordane county in western Norway, on the road linking Oslo to Bergen. During a trip in 2018, we used it twice: first to explore the region, Flåm, the fjord, and the Stegastein footbridge; and second to visit our colleague at the hospital in Bergen. The tunnel is divided into four sections separated by three large caverns carved into the mountain, which break up the monotony, providing a soothing and luminous view reminiscent of the Northern Lights, and allowing for U-turns. While the main tunnel is lit white, the caves are illuminated blue with yellow lights around the perimeter to create the illusion of a sunrise or the Northern Lights. The Lærdal Tunnel is the first in the world to be equipped with an air treatment plant, located in a cavern 100 meters wide.

title: Laerdal Tunnel in Aurland
content: ## Longest road tunnel in the world features an air treatment plant and the illusion of daylight. The longest tunnel in the world extends 15.2 miles (24.5 km) between the cities of Laerdal and Aurland in western Norway. Known as the Lærdal Tunnel (or Lærdalstunnelen in Norwegian), the tunnel's construction lasted five years and was completed in 2000, surpassing the world's second longest tunnel, the St. Gottard Tunnel in Switzerland, by five miles. Located in a 328-foot (100 m) cavern, the plant is comprised of two large fans and an electrostatic and carbon filter, which all work to remove dust and nitrogen dioxide from the large structure. The tunnel is thus divided into four different sections that are broken up by "mountain caves." The mountain caves are 3.7 miles (6 km) apart and each one is equipped with special lighting that gives off the illusion of driving into daylight.
